gaps.concept: Gender dysphoria requires at least six months of marked gender incongruence with clinically significant distress or impairment; transgender identity alone is not a disorder.
gaps.why_tested: A vignette asks whether gender incongruence without distress meets diagnostic criteria. [APA](https://www.psychiatry.org/patients-families/gender-dysphoria/what-is-gender-dysphoria)

gaps.concept: Continuous GnRH agonist exposure downregulates pituitary GnRH receptors, lowering LH, FSH, and gonadal sex steroids.
gaps.why_tested: Hormone results after puberty suppression require the drug mechanism. [Endocrine Society](https://www.endocrine.org/clinical-practice-guidelines/gender-dysphoria-gender-incongruence)

gaps.concept: Prolonged sex-steroid suppression during adolescence can reduce bone mineral accrual.
gaps.why_tested: A patient receiving puberty blockers has declining bone density. [Endocrine Society](https://www.endocrine.org/clinical-practice-guidelines/gender-dysphoria-gender-incongruence)

gaps.concept: Spironolactone antagonizes androgen receptors and reduces testosterone synthesis, in addition to blocking mineralocorticoid receptors.
gaps.why_tested: A question asks how a potassium-sparing drug contributes to feminization. [UCSF](https://transcare.ucsf.edu/guidelines/feminizing-hormone-therapy)

gaps.concept: Estradiol suppresses pituitary LH and FSH through negative feedback, lowering endogenous testicular testosterone production.
gaps.why_tested: A stem provides gonadotropin and testosterone levels during feminizing therapy. [Endocrine Society](https://www.endocrine.org/clinical-practice-guidelines/gender-dysphoria-gender-incongruence)

gaps.concept: Estrogen therapy can raise prolactin; new galactorrhea or headaches prompt consideration of hyperprolactinemia.
gaps.why_tested: A patient develops galactorrhea during feminizing therapy. [Endocrine Society](https://www.endocrine.org/clinical-practice-guidelines/gender-dysphoria-gender-incongruence)

gaps.concept: Feminizing hormones can reduce sperm production without reliably preventing pregnancy in a partner.
gaps.why_tested: A patient with retained testes asks whether estradiol provides contraception. [ACOG](https://www.acog.org/clinical/clinical-guidance/committee-opinion/articles/2021/03/health-care-for-transgender-and-gender-diverse-individuals)

gaps.concept: Testosterone can cause vaginal epithelial atrophy, dryness, and dyspareunia in patients with a retained vagina.
gaps.why_tested: A testosterone-treated patient reports painful intercourse and has thin vaginal mucosa. [ACOG](https://www.acog.org/clinical/clinical-guidance/committee-opinion/articles/2021/03/health-care-for-transgender-and-gender-diverse-individuals)

gaps.concept: Testosterone therapy can lower HDL and raise triglycerides.
gaps.why_tested: A lipid panel changes after masculinizing therapy. [ACOG](https://www.acog.org/clinical/clinical-guidance/committee-opinion/articles/2021/03/health-care-for-transgender-and-gender-diverse-individuals)

gaps.concept: After gonadectomy, stopping sex-steroid therapy increases bone-loss risk.
gaps.why_tested: A patient stops hormones after removal of the gonads and develops low bone density. [Endocrine Society](https://www.endocrine.org/clinical-practice-guidelines/gender-dysphoria-gender-incongruence)

gaps.concept: Gonorrhea and chlamydia NAAT specimens should come from exposed anatomic sites, including pharyngeal and rectal sites when relevant.
gaps.why_tested: A negative urine test misses infection after receptive oral or anal sex. [CDC](https://www.cdc.gov/std/treatment-guidelines/trans.htm)

gaps.concept: HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis is an option based on exposure risk regardless of gender identity or gender-affirming hormone use.
gaps.why_tested: A sexually active patient asks whether hormone therapy changes HIV prevention options. [CDC](https://www.cdc.gov/hivnexus/hcp/prep/index.html)

gaps.concept: Patients taking testosterone who can become pregnant may use effective contraception, including an IUD or progestin method.
gaps.why_tested: A patient with amenorrhea on testosterone wants pregnancy prevention. [ACOG](https://www.acog.org/clinical/clinical-guidance/committee-opinion/articles/2021/03/health-care-for-transgender-and-gender-diverse-individuals)

gaps.concept: Contraceptive sabotage, pregnancy pressure, and forced sex are forms of reproductive coercion that undermine voluntary consent.
gaps.why_tested: A partner removes condoms or pressures a patient into pregnancy. [ACOG](https://www.acog.org/clinical/clinical-guidance/committee-opinion/articles/2013/02/reproductive-and-sexual-coercion)

gaps.concept: Adolescent confidentiality has limits for mandated reporting or serious safety threats; insurance explanations of benefits can inadvertently disclose care.
gaps.why_tested: A minor seeks confidential STI care but fears parental notification through billing. [CDC](https://www.cdc.gov/std/treatment-guidelines/adolescents.htm)

gaps.concept: A patient's voluntary, informed preference governs permanent contraception; age, parity, or partner pressure alone must not determine the decision.
gaps.why_tested: A clinician must respond to a young patient's sterilization request or a partner's demand. [ACOG](https://www.acog.org/clinical/clinical-guidance/committee-statement/articles/2024/02/permanent-contraception-ethical-issues-and-considerations)
